message.content:
### Quick‑start – Kill **VS Code** (`code.exe`) from CMD/PowerShell | Command | What it does | |---------|--------------| | `taskkill /im code.exe /f` | Find *any* running instance(s) whose image name is `code.exe` and forcefully end them. | | `taskkill /im code.exe /t /f` | Same as above **plus** kills all child processes spawned by those `code.exe` instances (e.g., extensions, node workers). | --- #### Step‑by‑step guide ```cmd :: 1️⃣ List all running VS Code processes (optional but handy) tasklist | findstr /i code.exe ``` Output looks something like this: ``` Image Name PID Session Name Session# Mem Usage ========================= ======== =================== ========= ============ code.exe 12345 Console 0 15,432 K code.exe 67890 Console 0 9,876 K ``` If you only care about terminating everything at once, skip to step 2. Otherwise pick the specific PID(s). ```cmd :: 2️⃣ Terminate one particular instance taskkill /pid 12345 /f :: forces shutdown of PID 12345 :: 3️⃣ Or terminate ALL instances + their children taskkill /im code.exe /t /f ``` ##### Why `/t`? Visual Studio Code spawns several helper processes (extension hosts, Node.js workers, telemetry daemons…). Using `/t` ensures those get killed too—otherwise you’ll see stray “code” processes lingering after the main window closes. --- ### Common gotchas & tips | Issue | Fix / Recommendation | |-------|----------------------| | Unsaved files lost | Use normal exit (`File → Exit`) whenever possible. Only resort to `taskkill` when VS Code hangs. | | Multiple users/processes | If you're on a shared machine, double‑check which `code.exe` belongs to your session before forcing it. | | Permissions | Running `taskkill /f` requires administrative rights **only** if the target process runs under another account. In most cases, a standard user can stop their own VS Code instance. | | Batch file | You can wrap the command in a `.bat` file:
`@echo off\ncls\ntaskkill /im code.exe /t /f >nul 2>&1\nexit`| --- ### Alternative: PowerShell If you prefer PowerShell over plain CMD, the equivalent is even shorter: ```powershell Stop-Process -Name code -Force # stops all code.exe instances ``` or to mimic `/t` behaviour: ```powershell Get-Process code | % { $_.Id } | foreach { Get-WmiObject Win32_Process -Filter "ParentProcessID=$_" | Select-Object ProcessId | Foreach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force } } Stop-Process -Name code -Force ``` (That last block walks down the parent–child tree so no orphaned helpers remain.) --- ### TL;DR Just hit: ```cmd taskkill /im code.exe /t /f ``` …and voilà—you’ve shut down VS Code and its entire family of background tasks. Remember: do this only when the editor isn’t responding normally!
